5. We must find P(T < 8|T > 7).

Notice that by the rule of complement events, P(T < 8|T > 7) = 1 – P(T > 8|T > 7).

By the memoryless property (P(X > r + t|X > r) = P(X > t)).

So P(T > 8|T > 7) = P(T > 1) = 1–(1–e–18)=e–18≈0.8825" role="presentation" style="position: relative;">1–(1–e–18)=e–18≈0.8825\(1–(1–{e}^{–\frac{1}{8}})={e}^{–\frac{1}{8}}≈0.8825\)

Therefore, P(T < 8|T > 7) = 1 – 0.8825 = 0.1175.

Let X = the number of no-hitters throughout a season. Since the duration of time between no-hitters is exponential, the number of no-hitters per season is Poisson with mean λ = 3.

Therefore, (X = 0) = 30e–30!" role="presentation" style="position: relative;">30e–30!\(\frac{{3}^{0}{e}^{–3}}{0!}\) = e^(–3) ≈ 0.0498

  NOTE

You could let T = duration of time between no-hitters. Since the time is exponential and there are 3 no-hitters per season, then the time between no-hitters is 13" role="presentation" style="position: relative;">13\(\frac{1}{3}\) season. For the exponential, µ = 13" role="presentation" style="position: relative;">13\(\frac{1}{3}\).

Therefore, m = 1μ" role="presentation" style="position: relative;">1μ\(\frac{1}{μ}\) = 3 and T ∼ Exp(3).

1. The desired probability is P(T > 1) = 1 – P(T < 1) = 1 – (1 – e^(–3)) = e^(–3) ≈ 0.0498.

2. Let T = duration of time between no-hitters. We find P(T > 2|T > 1), and by the memoryless property this is simply P(T > 1), which we found to be 0.0498 in part a.

3. Let X = the number of no-hitters is a season. Assume that X is Poisson with mean λ = 3. Then P(X > 3) = 1 – P(X ≤ 3) = 0.3528.

1. P(T < 2) = 1 - 1−e−27" role="presentation" style="position: relative;">1−e−27\(1−{e}^{−\frac{2}{7}}\) ≈ 0.2485.

3. P(T > 15|T > 10) = P(T > 5) = 1−(1−e−57)=e−57≈0.4895" role="presentation" style="position: relative;">1−(1−e−57)=e−57≈0.4895\(1−(1−{e}^{−\frac{5}{7}})={e}^{−\frac{5}{7}}≈0.4895\).

4. Let X = # of patients arriving during a half-hour period. Then X has the Poisson distribution with a mean of 307" role="presentation" style="position: relative;">307\(\frac{30}{7}\), X ∼ Poisson(307)" role="presentation" style="position: relative;">(307)\((\frac{30}{7})\).
